anomalies.observed: C6 is a capacitor (value "0.1uF", libsource Device:C, description "Unpolarized capacitor") but its footprint is "Inductor_SMD:L_0805_2012Metric_Pad1.05x1.20mm_HandSolder", an inductor land pattern. In addition, only pin 2 is attached (to GND); pin 1 sits on the floating net "unconnected-(C6-Pad1)".
anomalies.expected: A capacitor should carry a capacitor footprint (e.g. C_0805_2012Metric...) and, as a decoupling/filter element, both terminals should be connected between a rail and GND.
anomalies.impact: C6 cannot perform any decoupling/filtering function because one terminal is open, so whatever node/rail it was meant to decouple loses its capacitor; the wrong (inductor) land pattern also risks wrong part placement/assembly.

anomalies.observed: SKW92A pins 13 and 14 (symbol function names LAN_PORT3_TX+ and LAN_PORT3_TX-) are both tied directly to the GND net, while the other PHY/GPIO pins are used for the keyboard/SD/EPD functions.
anomalies.expected: Unused module pins should be left open or handled per the module's own pin-share guidance rather than shorted; shorting a differential transmit pair to ground is not standard practice.
anomalies.impact: If the module's internal PHY still drives these pins, tying them to ground shorts the outputs (excess current/possible damage); otherwise the pins are simply held low. Either way they are unusable.

parsed.summary: The power, regulator, SKW92A, keyboard, microSD, EPD boost/inverter and load-switch sections all match the specification's stated connectivity and values, but C6 is a 0.1uF capacitor placed on an inductor land pattern with its pin 1 left floating (so it does nothing), and the SKW92A pins 13/14 are shorted to GND, so the build is not a clean copy of the intended design.

Flying node X = Net-(U6-K) = C10.1 side. C10.2 connects to SW (Net-(Q3-D)).

SW node voltage: In a boost, SW swings between ~0 (when Q3 on) and ~Vout (when Q3 off), where Vout is the boost output at J6.21.

Case A: Q3 on → SW ≈ 0V (actually ≈ I*Rds, near 0).
Case B: Q3 off → SW rises until U9 conducts, so SW ≈ Vout + 0.4.

During the transition B→A, SW drops from Vout+0.4 to 0. The cap C10 keeps its voltage, so X drops by (Vout+0.4). If X was at +0.4 (clamped by U7 during case B), then in case A X = 0.4 - (Vout+0.4) = -Vout. So X ≈ -Vout (negative). U6: anode = VGL (The net-(U6-A)), cathode = X = -Vout. So VGL > X, U6 conducts, current flows VGL → X, pulling VGL down toward X + 0.4 = -Vout + 0.4.
